correctness.rationale: Exact two-atom SIR initial data sum to one and all rates positive. Pressure transform gives I=1-S-gamma x and incidence derivative dC/dt=I[H(H-gamma)-IK]. A standalone exact Fraction interval certificate proves Q signs (+,-,+,-) at x=0,1/50,1/20,1/5 and H(1/5)>4/5. Since H is decreasing, I grows throughout this pressure interval, remains positive, and visits all sign points in finite time. Analytic sign changes force at least two strict local incidence maxima separated by a strict minimum. All strict inequalities persist on an open parameter neighborhood. Finite computation supplies only exact pointwise signs; the analytic proof supplies all quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Previously reported multiple waves are explicitly credited. The 2026 source supplies the SIR equations without describing aggregate incidence bimodality. Bootsma et al. 2024 exhibits double incidence peaks via heterogeneous latent periods or community interaction, Siegenfeld et al. 2022 with substantial connectivity separation, and Zheng et al. 2017 using multilayer delays. Directly examined material does not establish two fixed susceptibility classes with homogeneous infectiousness and pooled infectives producing multiple incidence peaks during strictly increasing prevalence. The exact constructive combination is not a special case of those stated results. Residual coverage by unindexed general multi-type theorems is expressly acknowledged; neither partitioning nor failed searches prove originality.
residual_risks: The multiwave phenomenon broadly predates this example. A general result not indexed under incidence or susceptible-class terminology might imply the restricted construction.
Mukherjee–Mondal–Bagchi (2021) primary full article was not materially accessible; only abstract and publisher preview could be compared.
The demonstrated incidence trough is shallow, so an epidemiological second-wave interpretation is not established.

value.rationale: A widely motivated mathematical distinction is whether more than one incidence peak needs interventions, delayed transmission, weakly coupled communities or a second prevalence rise. This robust exact-rational example proves that even only fixed two-atom susceptibility, homogeneous infectiousness and one well-mixed infectious pool suffice for two incidence peaks before its unique prevalence apex. The open-neighborhood and pressure ordering make the claim structural; a threshold/counterexample value need not yield a full peak-count census. The result is mathematically informative but not necessarily clinically large due to shallow trough.
